**Part 2: Jotto Activity (25 min)**

**Part 4: Binary Trees & Recursion (20 min)**

- Binary tree definition and recursive structure
- Height/node count relationship

- Preview BSTs (Wednesday)

## Let's Play Wordle! {.activity}

I'm thinking of a 5-letter word.

You have **6 guesses**.

After each guess, I'll tell you:

- 🟩 Green: Right letter, right position
- 🟨 Yellow: Right letter, wrong position
- ⬜ Gray: Letter not in word

**Let's play as a class!**

::: notes
Actually play 2-3 rounds with the class. Pick words ahead of time. Have students suggest guesses, vote on which to try. Track remaining possibilities on the board. Good words to use: CRANE, SLATE, MOIST, CHARM, PLUMB (words with common letters for game 1, then trickier ones).
:::

## {background-iframe="https://www.nytimes.com/games/wordle/index.html" background-interactive="true"}

::: notes
If you have internet, you can play the actual game. Otherwise, run it manually on the board.
:::

## What Strategy Did We Use?

Think about how we played:

- What made a guess "good"?
- How did we narrow down possibilities?
- Did we have a system, or was it intuition?

## The Strategy Question

Every guess **splits** the remaining possibilities.

| Guess | Feedback | Words eliminated |
|-------|----------|------------------|
| CRANE | ⬜🟨⬜⬜🟩 | Most words without R and E in those spots |
| STORE | 🟩⬜🟩🟨🟩 | Now we know S, O, E positions + R somewhere |
| ... | ... | ... |

**Good guesses split possibilities evenly.**

## Visualizing the Strategy

What if we drew every possible game?

```
                         SALET (first guess)
                        /       |        \        ...
                 🟩⬜⬜⬜⬜    🟨⬜⬜⬜⬜    🟩🟩⬜⬜⬜     ...
                    /           |            \
      SHIRK, SHOWY, SPICY   CRISP, MUSIC   SAPPY, SANDY
      SWORN, SNOWY, ...     PRISM, ...     SAUCY, ...
```

Each follow-up guess is **consistent** with prior feedback.

Each path from top to bottom is one game. This is a **tree**!

## The Wordle Decision Tree

This structure has a name: a **decision tree**.

- **Root**: First guess
- **Branches**: Possible feedback patterns (there are  \_\_\_\_\_\_\_)
- **Internal nodes**: Follow-up guesses
- **Leaves**: The answer (game over!)

The **height** of this tree = worst-case guesses needed.

## The Optimal Strategy Question

**Question**: What first guess gives the *best* tree?

What does best mean?

Research answer: **SALET**, **REAST**, **CRATE**, **TRACE**


## 3-Letter Jotto: Let's Build a Strategy {.activity .smaller}

**The setup:**

- There are 16 possible secret words 
- You guess a word; the response is the count of letters in common (0, 1, 2, or 3)
- You can only guess words that are still consistent with previous responses

**Your task:** Design a strategy — an algorithm that tells you what to guess in every situation, for any secret word.

**Specify your strategy:**

1. What's your **first guess**?
2. For each possible response (0, 1, 2, or 3), what do you guess **next**?
3. And so on, until you've identified the secret word.

## Jotto Scoring Examples

| Secret | Guess | Score | Why |
|--------|-------|-------|-----|
| FOX | JOG | 1 | O matches |
| DEW | YAK | 0 | No letters in common |
| NIP | INK | 2 | I and N match |
| WOO | MOB | 1 | O matches (counted once) |

## The 16 Words

```
DEW  FOX  GEL  INK
JOG  MOB  NAP  NIP
NOR  NUT  OAT  OIL
PUG  SOY  WOO  YAK
```

::: notes
Hand out card decks. Give students 5-7 minutes to play a few rounds, then regroup to discuss strategy.

Key questions to seed:
- What's a good first guess? Why?
- Did anyone try guessing similar words in a row (CAT, BAT, HAT)? How did that go?
- What's the worst case — how many guesses could it take?
:::

## What Strategy Did You Discover?

Discussion questions:

- What makes a "good" first guess?
- What happens if you guess CAT, then BAT, then HAT?
- Can you **always** win in 2 guesses? Why or why not?

::: notes
Lead into: the strategy IS a tree! Each guess partitions the remaining words by their Jotto score (0, 1, 2, or 3). Good guesses split evenly. Bad guesses leave big partitions.

Lower bound discussion: With 4 outcomes per guess and 16 words, theoretically log₄(16) = 2 guesses should suffice. But no word achieves a perfect 4-way split!
:::

## Why Trees?

Trees appear everywhere in computer science:

| Domain | Tree Structure |
|--------|---------------|
| File systems | Directories contain subdirectories |
| HTML/DOM | Elements contain child elements |
| Decision making | Each choice leads to sub-choices |
| Classification | "Is it X? If yes, go left..." |
| Game AI | Possible moves branch into more moves |

## Tree Terminology {.smaller}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="35%"}
```{=html}
<svg viewBox="0 0 320 300" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="max-width: 280px;">
  <!-- Tree: a(root) -> b -> (c,d), c -> (e,f), d -> g -> h -> (i,j) -->
  <!-- Structure gives: b, g, h have parent but no sibling = "bgh" -->
  <!-- Edges -->
  <line x1="160" y1="20" x2="160" y2="45" stroke="#333" stroke-width="2"/>
  <line x1="160" y1="65" x2="80" y2="100" stroke="#333" stroke-width="2"/>
  <line x1="160" y1="65" x2="240" y2="100" stroke="#333" stroke-width="2"/>
  <line x1="80" y1="120" x2="40" y2="155" stroke="#333" stroke-width="2"/>
  <line x1="80" y1="120" x2="120" y2="155" stroke="#333" stroke-width="2"/>
  <line x1="240" y1="120" x2="240" y2="155" stroke="#333" stroke-width="2"/>
  <line x1="240" y1="175" x2="240" y2="210" stroke="#333" stroke-width="2"/>
  <line x1="240" y1="230" x2="200" y2="265" stroke="#333" stroke-width="2"/>
  <line x1="240" y1="230" x2="280" y2="265" stroke="#333" stroke-width="2"/>

  <!-- Nodes -->
  <circle cx="160" cy="20" r="16" fill="white" stroke="#333" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="160" y="25" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13">a</text>

  <circle cx="160" cy="65" r="16" fill="white" stroke="#333" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="160" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13">b</text>

  <circle cx="80" cy="120" r="16" fill="white" stroke="#333" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="80" y="125" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13">c</text>

  <circle cx="240" cy="120" r="16" fill="white" stroke="#333" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="240" y="125" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13">d</text>

  <circle cx="40" cy="175" r="16" fill="white" stroke="#333" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="40" y="180" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13">e</text>

  <circle cx="120" cy="175" r="16" fill="white" stroke="#333" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="120" y="180" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13">f</text>

  <circle cx="240" cy="175" r="16" fill="white" stroke="#333" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="240" y="180" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13">g</text>

  <circle cx="240" cy="230" r="16" fill="white" stroke="#333" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="240" y="235" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13">h</text>

  <circle cx="200" cy="280" r="16" fill="white" stroke="#333" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="200" y="285" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13">i</text>

  <circle cx="280" cy="280" r="16" fill="white" stroke="#333" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="280" y="285" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13">j</text>
</svg>
```
:::
::: {.column width="65%"}
- One of the vertices is called the [root]{.red} of the tree. Guess which one it is.
- Make an English word containing the names of the vertices that have a [parent]{.red} but no [sibling]{.red}.
- How many [parents]{.red} does each vertex have?
- Which vertex has the fewest [children]{.red}?
- Which vertex has the most [ancestors]{.red}? [descendants]{.red}?
- What is d's [depth]{.red}? What is d's [height]{.red}?
- List all the vertices in b's left [subtree]{.red}.
- List all the [leaves]{.red} in the tree.
:::
:::

```{=html}
</svg>
```
:::
::: {.column width="65%"}
- [root]{.red}: the single node with no parent
- [leaf]{.red}: a node with no children
- [child]{.red}: a node pointed to by me
- [parent]{.red}: the node that points to me
- [sibling]{.red}: another child of my parent
- [ancestor]{.red}: my parent or my parent's ancestor
- [descendant]{.red}: my child or my child's descendant
- [subtree]{.red}: a node and its descendants
- [depth]{.red} of node x: number of edges on path from root to x
- [height]{.red} of node x: number of edges on longest path from x to a leaf
:::
:::

- \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_
